Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking this on. As part of our SOC 2 review and an upcoming SIG submission, our internal audit team has a focused set of asks around key management and HSM controls. To keep this scoped and avoid chasing multiple threads, can you provide the following artifacts (or indicate owners and ETA):

1) Rotation logs for master/wrapping keys covering the last 90 days (UTC timestamps). We need time-of-rotation, operator account, and audit-hash reference.
2) A copy of the current KMS policy (JSON) and the HSM seal attestation for the most recent rotation.
3) BYOK handshake traces for tenant handshakes (sample of 3 tenants, redacted as needed).
4) Evidence of secure key deletion/eviction for retired ephemeral keys in the last 12 months.
5) Access matrix showing which internal roles can perform rotate/unwrap/backup operations and separation-of-duties controls.

Can you confirm what you can provide by EOD Tuesday? If some artifacts are sensitive we can accept a short windowed Drive link or an SFTP drop. Happy to set a quick call if useful.

Regards,
Elena Vargas
Senior Compliance Manager
Bluecrest Financial

Marissa / Elena — tagging in a couple of technical notes so expectations are aligned:

- Rotation logs: we can supply a CSV extract with these columns: rotation_timestamp_utc, key_id, operator_principal, action, rotation_hash, previous_key_fingerprint. Example row (redacted):
  2029-04-29T03:12:07Z, wrap-key-3f7a, admin:jonas, rotate, ab12cd34..., f0e1d2c3...

- HSM attestation: we have a sealed PDF from the HSM vendor (FIPS-backed) for the 2029-05-01 ceremony. That will be included as hsm-seal-attestation-20290501.pdf.

- BYOK handshake: for tenant samples we will sanitize identifiers and provide handshake logs with session start/finish timestamps and KEK wrapping metadata. Note that some ingress logs contain IPs — we will redact those per our privacy policy. File: byok-handshake-sample.log (redacted).

- Secure deletion: our runner emits key-eviction records; the evidence is a combination of the eviction_event row and the zeroize-confirmation hash. We will produce a concise summary (one-page) plus a CSV of eviction events.

I'll attach the interim CSVs to the Drive link Marissa creates. If Bluecrest needs a hash-of-hashes for chain-of-custody verification, we can compute that; confirm desired algorithm (sha256 preferred).

-Jonas
